subject: Future Tech
title: Utah Arrays Explained
description: A short lesson to help you apply Utah Arrays Explained.

hook.text: The Utah Array is a tiny silicon chip with 100 needle-like electrodes that pierce the brain's outer layer.

buildup.text: Each needle records from a handful of neurons. Together the array captures a small neighborhood of brain activity.

discovery.text: Utah Arrays powered the BrainGate trials. They let paralyzed people control cursors and robotic arms with thought.

twist.text: The body attacks the array as a foreign object. Scar tissue forms around it, degrading signals within a few years.

climax.text: Despite that limitation, the Utah Array remains the most widely used invasive BCI electrode in human research.

punchline.text: One hundred needles opened the door to mind control.
